'''Diana S. Aga''' is a Filipino-American chemist who is the Henry M. Woodburn Chair in the Chemistry Department at the [[University at Buffalo]]. In 2023, she named a [[State University of New York|SUNY]] Distinguished Professor.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The State University of New York Distinguished Academy Class of 2023 |url=https://www.suny.edu/distinguished-academy/classes/2023/ }}</ref> Aga is the director of UB's Research and Education in Energy, Environment and Water (RENEW) Institute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Focus |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/renew/about-us/our-focus.html |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=www.buffalo.edu |language=en}}</ref> At the [[University at Buffalo]], she named her laboratory in the Chemistry Department at the University - the Aga Laboratory for Environmental Research and Testing (ALERT).<ref>{{Cite web |title=ALERT |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/renew/research/alert--aga-lab-for-environmental-research-and-testing.html |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=www.buffalo.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Education ==
Aga obtained a bachelor's in [[agricultural chemistry]] from the [[University of the Philippines Los Baños]]in 1988.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=KORNBERG 10/28/02 5:00am|first=SCOTT|title=Up Close and Personal With UB Professor Diana S. Aga|url=https://www.ubspectrum.com/article/2002/10/up-close-and-personal-with-ub-professor-diana-s-aga|access-date=2020-11-01|website=www.ubspectrum.com}}</ref> She earned a Ph.D from the [[University of Kansas]]. For her Ph.D, she researched applications of [[immunoassay]]s in agricultural chemistry.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Analytical applications of immunoassays in environmental and agricultural chemistry: study of the fate and transport of herbicides|date=1995|language=en|first=Diana S|last=Aga|oclc=43821680}}</ref> After graduating, she worked briefly for the [[United States Geological Survey]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Diana S. Aga|url=https://arts-sciences.buffalo.edu/chemistry/faculty/faculty-directory/aga.html|access-date=2020-11-01|website=arts-sciences.buffalo.edu|language=en}}</ref> and then joined [[ETH Zurich]] as a postdoctoral scholar for two years.

== Research and career ==
After a brief spell in industry, Aga returned to academia, and was appointed to the faculty at the [[University at Buffalo]] in 2002.<ref name=":1" /> In 2000, Aga was awarded an [[National Science Foundation CAREER Awards|National Science Foundation CAREER Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=NSF Award Search: Award#0233700 - CAREER: Immunochemical Techniques for Investigations on the Occurrence and Fate of Agrochemicals in the Environment|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0233700|access-date=2020-11-01|website=www.nsf.gov}}</ref>

Aga does [[mass spectroscopy]] analysis to obtain detailed information on chemical composition and information on compounds in materials.  She is one of many scientists worldwide who have applied this [[mass spectroscopy]] technique to investigate pesticides in crops,<ref name=":1" /> contaminants in ground and wastewater,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emerging contaminants to be examined by UB professor at seminar {{!}} Fredonia.edu|url=https://www.fredonia.edu/news/articles/emerging-contaminants-be-examined-ub-professor-seminar|access-date=2020-11-01|website=www.fredonia.edu}}</ref> presence of antibiotics in wastewater,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Diana Aga: Faculty Expert in Chemical Pollution - University at Buffalo|url=http://www.buffalo.edu/news/experts/diana-aga-faculty-expert-chemical-pollution.html|access-date=2020-11-02|website=www.buffalo.edu|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Cleaning up a breeding ground for antimicrobial resistance|url=http://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2015/10/023.html|access-date=2020-11-02|website=www.buffalo.edu|language=en}}</ref> chemical compositions of brominated flame retardants([[polybrominated diphenyl ethers]], BDEs) which are toxic chemicals.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Shedding light on potential toxins that lurk in blood and breast milk|url=http://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2015/09/032.html|access-date=2020-11-02|website=www.buffalo.edu|language=en}}</ref> Aga has co-authored a paper describing the presence of pharmaceuticals, in particular antidepressants, in Great Lakes fish.<ref name="10.1021_acs.est.7b02912">{{Cite journal |last1=Arnnok |first1=Prapha |last2=Singh |first2=Randolph R. |last3=Burakham |first3=Rodjana |last4=Pérez-Fuentetaja |first4=Alicia |last5=Aga |first5=Diana S. |date=2017-09-19 |title=Selective Uptake and Bioaccumulation of Antidepressants in Fish from Effluent-Impacted Niagara River |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.est.7b02912 |journal=Environmental Science & Technology |language=en |volume=51 |issue=18 |pages=10652–10662 |doi=10.1021/acs.est.7b02912 |issn=0013-936X|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lee |first=Bruce Y. |title=Antidepressants Found In The Great Lakes And Fish |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/brucelee/2017/09/04/antidepressants-found-in-the-great-lakes-and-fish/ |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=Forbes |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lohan |first=Tara |date=2021-08-11 |title=What Happens to Wildlife Swimming in a Sea of Our Drug Residues? • The Revelator |url=https://therevelator.org/wildlife-water-pharmaceuticals/ |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=The Revelator |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==

* 2007 New York Water Environment Association's, Kenneth Allen Memorial Award given annually for papers or presentations describing work of a research or engineering nature including papers with multiple co-authors <ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title= New York Water Environment Association's Awards|url=https://www.nywea.org/membership/awards/ }}</ref>
* 2013 [[University at Buffalo]] Excellence in Graduate Student Mentoring Award given on an annual basis, to a member of the UB Graduate Faculty.<ref>{{Cite web |title= UB's Excellence in Graduate Student Mentoring Award |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/grad/intranet/onboarding/rfp/mentoring-award.html }}</ref>
* 2022 [[American Chemical Society]] Fellow cited for "Recognized for encouraging women and underrepresented minority students to pursue careers in environmental and agricultural chemistry and for innovative contributions in agrochemical analysis to better understand their ecological and health impacts."<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 ACS Fellows |url=https://www.acs.org/funding/awards/acs-fellows/fellows/2022-fellows.html |access-date=2024-02-22 |website=American Chemical Society |language=en}}</ref>
* 2024 Analytical Scientist Power List, Aga is ranked #8 in "Planet Protector" field.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-17 |title=The Power List 2024 |url=https://theanalyticalscientist.com/power-list/2024 |access-date=2024-08-24 |website=The Analytical Scientist |language=en}}</ref>
